response_json.text:
If you’re shopping for a **new luxury SUV in the U.S. right now**, I’d prioritize **manufacturer-subsidized financing** over a generic bank loan when the APR is genuinely low. Current offers show some unusually attractive rates. ([CarEdge](https://caredge.com/guides/deals/luxury/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Best options I’d look at

| SUV | Current advertised financing | My take |
|---|---:|---|
| **BMW X5** | **0.9% up to 60 mo.** + $1,000 purchase credit on select models | ⭐ Excellent |
| **BMW X3** | **0.9% up to 60 mo.** on select models | ⭐ Excellent |
| **BMW X7** | **0.9%** on select models | ⭐ Excellent |
| **Cadillac VISTIQ** | **0.9% up to 72 mo.** + $2,000 allowance | ⭐ Excellent if EV |
| **Infiniti QX80** | **0% for 60 mo.** + $3,000 cash incentive reported | ⭐ Potentially best deal |
| **Lexus RX/NX** | ~**2.99%** | Very good |
| **Mercedes GLE** | ~**3.99%** on current manufacturer offer | Good |
| **Cadillac Escalade IQ** | ~**2.9%** on select models | Good |

BMW's published offers, for example, show **0.90% APR up to 60 months on the X5**, along with a $1,000 purchase credit on qualifying X5s. ([BMW USA](https://www.bmwusa.com/special-offers/finance.2025-M340i-xDrive-Sedan.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) Cadillac is advertising **0.9% on qualifying VISTIQs**, while its current offers also include 2.9% financing on certain models. ([Cadillac](https://www.cadillac.com/offers/current?x-zipcode=90210&utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### [BMW X5](https://www.phoenixcarsjapan.com/products/2026_25150220?utm_campaign=openai_catalog&utm_content=product_card&utm_medium=feed&variant=54645865578806&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
*$65,064.84*

### [BMW X3](https://www.phoenixcarsjapan.com/products/2026_22950047?utm_campaign=openai_catalog&utm_content=product_card&utm_medium=feed&variant=54628732076342&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
*$44,108.37*

### [Mercedes-Benz GLE 350](https://starlingermotors.com/products/2026-mercedes-benz-gle-350-4matic-4jgfb4fb4tb519500?utm_campaign=openai_catalog&utm_content=product_card&utm_medium=feed&variant=48515270738164&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
*$68,116.00*

### [Audi Q8](https://www.phoenixcarsjapan.com/products/2026_17200004?utm_campaign=openai_catalog&utm_content=product_card&utm_medium=feed&variant=54646734782774&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
*$63,747.57*

### The financing strategy I'd use

**1. Get pre-approved through a credit union/bank first.**
That gives you a baseline rate and prevents the dealer from being your only financing option.

**2. Then ask the manufacturer for its promotional APR.**
Luxury manufacturers sometimes subsidize loans heavily. A 0.9% manufacturer loan can beat a bank loan by thousands.

**3. Compare APR *and* incentives.**
For example, **0.9% with a $1,000 rebate** can be better than 0% financing if the 0% deal requires you to surrender a much larger cash incentive.

**4. Don't automatically choose the longest term.**
At these low promotional rates, 60 months is often a sweet spot. At normal/high APRs, stretching a $70k–$100k SUV to 72–84 months can become expensive.

**5. Compare leasing too.**
For luxury SUVs, leasing can be surprisingly competitive because of manufacturer-supported residual values. Current examples include the BMW X5, Mercedes GLE, Lexus RX/NX and Acura MDX. ([TrueCar](https://www.truecar.com/deals/luxury-suvs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### If you give me your numbers

I can narrow this down to the **3–5 best luxury SUVs for your situation** and calculate the actual monthly payment and total interest.

Send me:
- **Budget:** e.g. $70k–$100k
- **Down payment:** e.g. $10k
- **Credit score:** approximate range
- **Buy or lease**
- **Preferred brands:** BMW, Mercedes, Lexus, Porsche, Range Rover, Cadillac, etc.
- **New or used**

Then I can compare **X5 vs. GLE vs. GX/LX vs. Escalade vs. Q8 vs. Range Rover**, including financing costs.
